newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania farm reforms run into trouble.
newsitem.headline: Romania farm reforms run into trouble.

text.p: Plans by Romania's new centrist government to overhaul the inefficient farming sector ran into trouble on Thursday when members of parliament rejected proposals to shut down or privatise 75 state farms.
A statement by the Agriculture Commission of parliament's upper house, the Senate, said members had thrown out the list of farms, saying each case had to be studied individually.
"The commission requests a detailed analysis of each state-run company in agriculture," the statement said after Wednesday's vote.
"Companies with low output and big losses for years could on this basis be earmarked for privatisation or liquidation."

The ministry issued the list of 75 loss-making state farms this month as part of plans to restructure the sector and reduce subsidies as demanded by the International Monetary Fund and other international lenders.

The World Bank has allocated a $250 million Agriculture Structural Adjustment Loan to help Romania revamp its farming sector. The IMF has made farm reform a vital element of its programme of credits for Romania worth $430 million.
Bad management and slow reform during seven years of government by leftists thrown out of office in last November's election have brought agriculture to the brink of collapse.
The Agriculture Ministry said the 75 farms had debts totalling 1.06 trillion lei ($150 million), or 39.9 percent of total losses of 2.66 trillion lei in the state farming sector last year.
Ministry officials were unavailable for comment. But a commission member told Reuters the ministry would have to review the list before submitting it to parliamentary debate.

The government has singled out as targets for change sprawling pig and poultry farms which in the seven years of post-communist rule maintained high production levels without regard to cost and and other factors.
Twenty such farms were to be sold off but buyers have been found so far for only five. Four have been closed down.

The government has also produced a list of 10 major loss-making industrial companies to be shut down, a move applauded by the IMF. But their closure has been delayed, subject to rescue plans mounted by their management.
